sanskrit: sahaiva vo hṛdayāni saha vijñānam astu vaḥ | sahendro vṛtrahā karat saha devo bṛhaspatiḥ ||
english: Together let your hearts be one, together let understanding be yours; together may Indra the slayer of Vṛtra act, together the god Bṛhaspati.

sanskrit: samānam astu vo hṛdayaṃ samānam uto vo manaḥ | samāno agnir vo devaḥ saha rāṣṭram upādhvam ||
english: Let your heart be one, and one likewise your mind; one the divine Agni among you — together hold your realm firm.

sanskrit: saṃ jānīdhvaṃ sahṛdayāḥ sarve saṃmanasa stha | naṣṭo vo manyur jīrṇerṣyā saha jīvātha bhadrayā ||
english: Come to accord, be of one heart, be all of one mind; your wrath is spent, worn-out jealousy is gone — live together in well-being.

sanskrit: yathā putraḥ pravāvadaḥ pitṛbhyāṃ vadati priyam | evā yūyam anyo 'nyasmai jihvayā vadata priyam ||
english: As a son who speaks freely says what is dear to his parents, so shall you speak what is dear to one another with your tongues.

sanskrit: sahaiva vo dhānyāni samānāḥ paśavaś ca vaḥ | saha pṛthivyāṃ vīrudhaḥ saha vaḥ santv oṣadhīḥ ||
english: Together let your stores of grain be one, and your cattle alike; together let the plants grow for you on the earth, together let the herbs be yours.

sanskrit: saha dīkṣā saha yajño vivāho vaḥ sahāsati | saha prapharvā nṛtyantu saha va striya āsatām ||
english: Together let your consecration and sacrifice be, your marriage in common dwelling; together let the revelers dance, together let your women sit.

sanskrit: sahaiva vo vīryāṇi sahānyān randhayādhvai | saha patatriṇīm iṣum anyasmai hetim asyata ||
english: Together exercise your manly powers; together subdue your enemies; together shoot the winged arrow as a weapon against the foe.

sanskrit: saṃ vasyāmi samitiṃ madhunā vācam āñjiṣam | yuṣmākam anye śṛṇvantu- -uditaṃ saṅgate jane ||
english: I anoint the assembly with honey, I anoint speech; let others hear what is spoken among you in the gathered community.

sanskrit: yuṣmān mitrā vṛṇatāṃ yuṣmān pratijanā uta | yuṣmāt jñātitvaṃ prepsanty amṛtaṃ martyā iva ||
english: Let allies choose you; let the opposing clans choose you also; from you they seek kinship, as mortals seek immortality.

sanskrit: saṃsam id yaḥ sam ākaraṃ saha yūthā gavām iva | samānam astu vo mano jyeṣṭhaṃ vijñānam anv ita ||
english: I who have brought you together, as one herds the troops of cattle — let your mind be one; follow after the highest understanding.

sanskrit: idaṃ yad eṣāṃ hṛdayaṃ tad eṣāṃ hṛdaye bhavat | atho yad eṣāṃ hṛdayaṃ tad veṣāṃ hṛdi śritam | samānam astu vo manaḥ śreṣṭhaṃ vijñānam anv ita ||
english: This their heart — let it dwell in their heart; and further: this their heart — in their heart let it rest. Let your mind be one; follow after the most excellent understanding.

sanskrit: idaṃ yad eṣāṃ mana eṣāṃ yāni manāṃsi ca | sadhryag indra tat kṛṇu rathe pādāv ivāhitau ||
english: This mind of theirs, and whatever minds they have — make them all moving in one direction, O Indra, as two feet are set upon a chariot.

sanskrit: sahasrabāhuḥ puruṣaḥ sahasrākṣaḥ sahasrapāt | sa bhūmiṃ viśvato vṛtvā- -aty atiṣṭhad daśāṅgulam ||
english: The Puruṣa has a thousand arms, a thousand eyes, a thousand feet; he encompassed the earth on all sides and surpassed it by ten fingers' breadth.

sanskrit: tribhiḥ padbhir dyām arohat pād asyehābhavat punaḥ | tathā vy akrāmad viṣvaṅṅ aśanānaśane anu ||
english: With three of his feet he ascended the sky; one foot of his remained here again; thence he strode forth in every direction over what feeds and what feeds not.

sanskrit: tāvanto asya mahimānas tato jyāyāṃś ca puruṣaḥ | pād asya viśvā bhūtāni tripād asyāmṛtaṃ divi ||
english: Such are his grandeurs — and greater yet is the Puruṣa; one quarter of him is all beings, three quarters of him is the immortal in the sky.

sanskrit: puruṣa evedaṃ sarvaṃ yad bhūtaṃ yac ca bhāvyam | utāmṛtatvasyeśvaro yad annenābhavat saha ||
english: The Puruṣa alone is all this — what has been and what shall be; he is the lord of immortality, he who has grown together with food.

sanskrit: yat puruṣaṃ vyadadhuḥ katidhā vy akalpayan | mukhaṃ kim asya kiṃ bāhū kim ūrū pādā ucyete ||
english: When they stretched out the Puruṣa, into how many parts did they divide him? What is called his mouth, what his arms, what his thighs and feet?

sanskrit: brāhmaṇo 'sya mukham āsīd bāhū rājanyo 'bhavat | madhyaṃ tad asya yad vaiśyaḥ padbhyāṃ śūdro ajāyata ||
english: The Brāhmaṇa was his mouth; the Rājanya became his arms; that which is his middle is the Vaiśya; from his feet the Śūdra was born.

sanskrit: virāḍ agre sam abhavad virājo adhi pūruṣaḥ | sa jāto aty aricyata paścād bhūmim atho puraḥ ||
english: Virāj first came into being; from Virāj the Puruṣa arose; having been born he spread beyond, backward across the earth and also forward.

sanskrit: yat puruṣeṇa haviṣā devā yajñam atanvata | vasanto asyāsīd ājyaṃ grīṣma idhmaḥ śarad dhaviḥ ||
english: When the gods performed the sacrifice with the Puruṣa as the oblation, spring was its clarified butter, summer its firewood, autumn its oblation.

sanskrit: taṃ yajñaṃ prāvṛṣā praukṣan puruṣaṃ jātam agraśaḥ | tena devā ayajanta sādhyā vasavaś ca ye ||
english: They sprinkled with the rains that sacrifice, that Puruṣa born in the beginning; with him the gods sacrificed — the Sādhyas and the Vasus.

sanskrit: tasmād aśvā ajāyanta ye ca ke cobhayādataḥ | gāvo ha jajñire tasmāt tasmāj jātā ajāvayaḥ ||
english: From him horses were born, and all those that have teeth on both jaws; from him cattle were born, and from him goats and sheep were born.

sanskrit: tasmād yajñāt sarvahuta ṛcaḥ sāmāni jajñire | chando ha jajñire tasmād yajus tasmād ajāyata ||
english: From that sacrifice offered entire, the Ṛc verses and the Sāman chants were born; the meters were born from it; the Yajus was born from it.

sanskrit: tasmād yajñāt sarvahutaḥ saṃbhṛtaṃ pṛṣadājyam | paśūn tāṃś cakre vāyavyān āraṇyān grāmyāś ca ye ||
english: From that sacrifice offered entire the speckled butter was brought together; he fashioned from it those animals that belong to the air, those of the forest and those of the village.

sanskrit: saptāsyāsan paridhayas triḥ sapta samidhaḥ kṛtāḥ | devā yad yajñaṃ tanvānā abadhnan puruṣaṃ paśum ||
english: Seven were its enclosing sticks; thrice seven were the kindling sticks made ready, when the gods, performing the sacrifice, bound the Puruṣa as the sacrificial beast.

sanskrit: mūrdhno devasya bṛhato 'ṃśavaḥ sapta saptatīḥ | rājñaḥ somasyājāyanta jātasya puruṣād adhi ||
english: From the head of the great divine one seven times seventy soma-shoots were born — of King Soma who arose from the Puruṣa when he was brought forth.

sanskrit: candramā manaso jātaś cakṣuḥ sūryo 'jāyata | śrotrād vāyuś ca prāṇaś ca mukhād agnir ajāyata ||
english: The moon was born from his mind; the sun was born from his eye; from his ear came Vāyu and Prāṇa; from his mouth Agni was born.

sanskrit: nābhyā āsīd antarikṣaṃ śīrṣṇo dyauḥ sam avartata | padbhyāṃ bhūmir diśaḥ śrotrāṅ tathā lokām̐ akalpayan ||
english: From his navel came the atmosphere; from his head the sky was fashioned; from his feet the earth, from his ears the directions — thus did they form the worlds.

sanskrit: imāṃ khanāmy oṣadhim adṛṣṭahananīm aham | aśvasyāvo dadāti tvā vairūpo vājinīvati ||
english: I dig up this herb that slays the invisible ones; the descendant of Aśva gives you this, O Vairūpa, in the plant-rich place.

sanskrit: nādṛṣṭā vo jihvāḥ santi na dantā hanvor adhi | nāpi madhyaṃ no śiras te yūyaṃ kiṃ kariṣyatha ||
english: You invisible ones have no tongues; there are no teeth in your jaws; you have neither a middle nor a head — what then will you do?

sanskrit: indrāmitrā indrahatā na va ihāsti nyañcanam | indro vaḥ sarvāsāṃ sākaṃ śakras tṛṇeḍhu vṛtrahā ||
english: O adṛṣṭas, enemies of Indra, slain by Indra — there is no refuge for you here; Indra, the mighty Śakra, slayer of Vṛtra, crushes all of you together.

sanskrit: aśvatarām̐ ayaḥśaphān yān indro adhitiṣṭhati | tair vo 'pi nahyeya te mukhāny udarasarpiṇaḥ ||
english: The mules with iron hooves upon which Indra rides — with those I would bind shut your mouths, O you that crawl in the belly.

sanskrit: apinahyam adṛṣṭānāṃ mukhaṃ pādā dṛter iva | utaiṣāṃ jihvā niṣkartā nirdantā hanvor adhi ||
english: I bind shut the mouth of the invisible ones, like the foot-opening of a skin bag; and their tongues shall be cut out, toothless in their jaws.

sanskrit: avadhiṣam asṛgādāṃ ni kroḍādā alipsata | abhaitsaṃ sarveṣām āṇḍāni ye adṛṣṭāḥ pṛthivīkṣitaḥ ||
english: I have struck down the blood-drinkers; the bosom-devourers I have fixed in place; I have shattered the eggs of all the invisible ones that dwell upon the earth.

sanskrit: riśyāsaḥ pauruṣāso darbhāso vairiṇā uta | mauñjā adṛṣṭāḥ sairyāḥ sarve sākaṃ ni jasyata ||
english: The riśyas, the pauruṣas, the darbhas, and those of hostile nature; the mauñjas, the invisible ones, the sairyas — let all of them be cast down together.

sanskrit: adṛṣṭānāṃ sapta jātā pṛthivī na śiśe mahī | tān indro bāhubhyāṃ sarvāñ chakro apāvayat ||
english: The seven kinds of invisible ones — the great earth does not bear them; Indra, the mighty, has swept all of them away with his arms.

sanskrit: ye vaḥ santi sapta jātā adṛṣṭāḥ puruṣādinaḥ | grāvṇāṃśūn iva somasya tān sarvān pra mṛṇīmasi ||
english: You who are the seven kinds of invisible man-devouring ones — we crush all of them as the pressing stones crush the soma stalks.

sanskrit: ya ātmajā ye vastijā ya ruṣā ya u todinaḥ | tebhyaḥ khanāmy oṣadhiṃ yebhyo bimbīvadhaḥ kṛtaḥ ||
english: Those born from the self, those born in the bladder, those born in anger, and those that pierce — for protection against them I dig up the herb for which the bimbi-plant is the slayer.

sanskrit: adṛṣṭebhyas taruṇebhyo yuvadbhya sthavirebhyaḥ | āhārṣam ugrām oṣadhiṃ yebhyo bimbīvadhaḥ kṛtaḥ ||
english: Against the invisible ones — the young, the adolescent, the aged — I have brought the fierce herb for which the bimbi-plant is the slayer.

sanskrit: ye ca dṛṣṭā ye cādṛṣṭās titīlāḥ śalunāś ca ye | tān agne sarvān saṃ daha krimīn anejato jahi ||
english: Those that are seen and those that are unseen, the titīlas and the śalunas — burn all of them, O Agni; slay the worms that do not tremble before you.
